To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

thyroid hormones were positively associated with heart rate, and PR interval in a linear or U-shape manner, and negatively associated with QRS in men and a U-shaped association was observed in women in the general population.
thyroid hormone levels in normal range were associated with various EKG changes.
variation in thyroid hormone levels, even within the reference range, was associated, in a dose-response manner, with various ECG findings in a large population-based sample of US adults.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how variations in thyroid hormones within the normal range may influence electrocardiographic parameters in the general population.
the relationship between the thyroid hormones and electrocardiographic parameters.
the relationship between thyroid hormone levels within a normal range and ECG changes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the thyroid hormone status of the general population affects the heart in various ways.

a higher level of thyroid hormone was positively associated with heart rate in men and a lower level of thyroid hormone appeared to be associated with shorter PR interval in men, and higher TSH was positively associated with longer QRS in men and a U-shaped association between TSH levels and QRS interval in women.
thyroid hormone level is associated with heart rate, PR, QRS, QT, and JT interval, but the association is not always linear.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
thyroid hormones have a significant impact on the heart, and the impact may be different in men and women and in different age groups.

the higher the T4, the higher the heart rate, the longer the QRS interval, and the longer the corrected QT and JT in men; and that the higher the serum T4, the longer the PR interval in men, and the longer PR and QRS intervals in women.
thyroid hormones affect the heart rate, PR interval, QRS duration and QT and JT intervals, but the effect is not linear.
The main takeaway from our work is that
even small changes in T4 or TSH levels may be associated with changes in heart rate and PR, QRS, and QT intervals.
the thyroid hormone status of an individual may have a significant impact on the heart rate and conduction velocity, and that this association may differ between men and women.
serum T4 and T4 levels are associated with heart rate, PR, and QRS intervals, and serum TSH is associated with QRS.
